mentions.quote: by those devoted to Viṣṇu
mentions.role: deity whose devotees have ritual obligations

mentions.quote: the blessed Lord Hari always sleeps on the serpent-couch in the ocean of milk
mentions.role: deity who undergoes cosmic sleep and awakening

mentions.quote: one should awaken the sleeping Keśava at night, full of faith and devotion
mentions.role: deity to be ritually awakened

mentions.quote: the turning of the side of Viṣṇu occurs, which destroys great sins
mentions.role: deity whose ritual turning-over is performed

mentions.quote: On the Ekādaśī of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, Janārdana is praised by the gods, ṛṣis, and hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases
mentions.role: deity praised on Ekādaśī

mentions.quote: the blessed Madhusūdana attains His own illusion, the yogic sleep, on the serpent's body
mentions.role: deity entering cosmic yogic sleep

mentions.quote: Viṣṇu sleeps in the first quarter of Maitra (Anurādhā), turns over in the middle of Śruti (Śravaṇa)
mentions.role: deity whose sleep, turning, and awakening correspond to nakṣatras

mentions.quote: Viṣṇu does not sleep during the day, nor does He awaken at night
mentions.role: subject of ritual timing regulation

mentions.quote: A mortal over eight years old, and not yet eighty, who eats in my kingdom on Viṣṇu's day, is a sinner
mentions.role: deity whose sacred day prohibits eating

entities.description: The deity Viṣṇu, referred to by multiple names, is the central figure of the Ekādaśī section—his cosmic sleep, turning over, and awakening structure the Cāturmāsya rituals, and his day (Ekādaśī) is the primary occasion for fasting obligations.
entities.justification: Viṣṇu appears by multiple names across dozens of paragraphs as the theological anchor of the Ekādaśī and Cāturmāsya discussions.

mentions.quote: The Navamī of the bright fortnight of Āśvina is Durgā-navamī
mentions.role: deity whose navamī is the occasion of the festival

mentions.quote: one should worship Durgā, the slayer of the buffalo demon
mentions.role: deity to be worshipped on Mahānavamī

mentions.quote: men should properly worship Aparājitā, facing the northeast direction, in the afternoon, with effort
mentions.role: deity worshipped on Vijayā-daśamī

mentions.quote: on it Aparājitā should be worshipped
mentions.role: deity of Vijayā-daśamī worship

entities.description: Durgā, also called Aparājitā ('the unconquered') and identified as the slayer of the buffalo demon, is the presiding deity of Durgā-navamī and Vijayā-daśamī, requiring ritual worship with specific directional and temporal prescriptions.
entities.justification: Durgā is explicitly named as the deity of Navamī and Daśamī festivals in multiple quoted Purāṇic verses.

mentions.quote: This regulation, stated by Mārkaṇḍeya, does exist
mentions.role: authoritative sage whose ruling on tithi-selection regulates ritual choice

mentions.quote: This is also from the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa
mentions.role: author of cited scriptural text

entities.description: Mārkaṇḍeya is cited as an authoritative sage whose regulation on accepting tithis in bright and dark fortnights resolves the otherwise unrestricted choice of Daśamī.
entities.justification: Mārkaṇḍeya is explicitly named as the source of a regulatory verse on tithi selection in paragraph p-9a294f.

mentions.quote: As for the verse of Nārada: The animal sacrifice is praised on Navamī in the afternoon
mentions.role: sage whose verse is cited on timing of animal sacrifice

mentions.quote: In every fortnight, a fast should be performed on Ekādaśī
mentions.role: scriptural authority enjoining Ekādaśī fasting

mentions.quote: This is from the statement of Nārada
mentions.role: sage whose verse prescribes fasting on Dvādaśī when Ekādaśī is extended

entities.description: Nārada is cited multiple times as an authoritative sage whose verses determine the timing of animal sacrifice on Navamī and the injunction to fast on Ekādaśī every fortnight.
entities.justification: Nārada is explicitly named as source for verses on Navamī sacrifice timing and the Ekādaśī fast injunction.

mentions.quote: The ten sins are stated by Manu as follows: Harshness, falsehood, and also slander of every kind
mentions.role: lawgiver who enumerates the ten sins removed by Daśaharā

entities.description: Manu is cited in a footnote-like explanatory passage as the authority who enumerates the ten sins (bodily, verbal, and mental) that Daśaharā is said to remove.
entities.justification: Manu is explicitly named as the source of the classification of ten sins in paragraph p-e3b90e.

mentions.quote: This is from a verse of Jaimini
mentions.role: Mīmāṃsā authority whose verse distinguishes occasion-prompted from context-prompted fasts

entities.description: Jaimini is cited as a Mīmāṃsā philosopher-authority whose verse on occasion-prompted versus non-occasion-prompted rites is used to reconcile apparently conflicting injunctions about Sunday fasting and Ekādaśī.
entities.justification: Jaimini is explicitly named as the author of a verse on ritual occasion in paragraph p-e18609.

mentions.quote: in the Bhaviṣya Purāṇa cited by Hemādri
mentions.role: digest-compiler whose citation is referenced

mentions.quote: This meaning is also accepted by Hemādri and others
mentions.role: commentator whose interpretation is endorsed

mentions.quote: the verse is accepted by all treatises, such as the Hemādri
mentions.role: authoritative digest that accepts the verse

mentions.quote: Hemādri, however, says that this verse is for the purpose of preventing the austerity of fasting until death
mentions.role: commentator whose interpretation is considered but not fully accepted

mentions.quote: Hemādri and others say that this verse is for the purpose of an exclusion for a householder with a son
mentions.role: commentator on exclusion of dark Ekādaśī

mentions.quote: This is from a verse cited by Hemādri
mentions.role: compiler citing a verse on optional Vaiṣṇava vow

entities.description: Hemādri is a medieval digest-compiler whose work (*Caturvargacintāmaṇi*) is repeatedly cited as an authoritative reference for Purāṇic verses and interpretive positions across tithi determination.
entities.justification: Hemādri is explicitly named six times as both compiler and commentator on questions of Ekādaśī fasting and Viṣṇu's sleep rituals.

mentions.quote: the interpretation of the Kalpataru, that Āṣāḍhī is Ekādaśī, and Kārttikī is Ekādaśī, is refuted
mentions.role: scholastic work whose interpretation is refuted (contextual)

mentions.quote: Mādhava and others say that this is for the purpose of indicating a greater fault for a householder with a son
mentions.role: commentator whose view is cited then rejected

mentions.quote: Mādhava and others say that it applies to those other than Vaiṣṇavas, by elimination
mentions.role: commentator on sūryodaya-vedha applicability

entities.description: Mādhava (likely Mādhavācārya) is cited as a commentator whose interpretations on Kṛṣṇa-ekādaśī prohibition and vedha applicability are engaged with and in some cases refuted.
entities.justification: Mādhava is named explicitly in paragraphs p-734770 and p-ff81dc as a commentator whose positions are evaluated by the Vīramitrodaya.

mentions.quote: This is from the statement of Devala
mentions.role: smṛti author whose verse distinguishes householder rights on Ekādaśī

entities.description: Devala is a smṛti authority whose verse distinguishing householders (bright fortnight only) from forest-dwellers and ascetics (both fortnights) for the Ekādaśī vow is cited and endorsed.
entities.justification: Devala is explicitly named as source of verse on Ekādaśī rights in paragraph p-4d78ca.

mentions.quote: This is from the statement of Kaśyapa
mentions.role: sage whose verse defines Vijayā-daśamī when Ekādaśī predominates

entities.description: Kaśyapa is cited as a sage-authority whose verse specifies that Vijayā-daśamī should be taken when Daśamī is present only briefly at sunrise and Ekādaśī is complete with Śravaṇa nakṣatra.
entities.justification: Kaśyapa is explicitly named in paragraph p-ef6ee4 as the source of the Vijayā-daśamī definition verse.

mentions.quote: This is from the statement of Kātyāyana
mentions.role: smṛti authority whose verse requires husband's consent for wife's vows

entities.description: Kātyāyana is a smṛti lawgiver whose verse requiring husbandly consent for a wife's vows and fasts is cited in the discussion of women's Ekādaśī rights.
entities.justification: Kātyāyana is explicitly named as source of the consent-verse in paragraph p-393353.

mentions.quote: This is from the statement of Vṛddha Yājñavalkya
mentions.role: elder smṛti authority whose verse resolves conflict of śrāddha and fast

entities.description: Vṛddha Yājñavalkya ('the elder Yājñavalkya') is cited as a smṛti authority whose verse instructs that when an obligatory fast coincides with an occasional śrāddha, the fast takes precedence (with smelling the food).
entities.justification: Vṛddha Yājñavalkya is explicitly named in paragraph p-23da73 as the source of the śrāddha-fast conflict resolution.

mentions.quote: And so, Yama says
mentions.role: deity-lawgiver whose verse on Viṣṇu's sleep on Āṣāḍhī is cited

entities.description: Yama, the deity of death and dharma, is cited as a smṛti-like authority whose verse states that Hari sleeps on Āṣāḍhī (full moon of Āṣāḍha) and awakens on Kārttikī.
entities.justification: Yama is explicitly named in paragraph p-50ba5f as the speaker of the verse on Viṣṇu's cosmic sleep.

mentions.quote: When there is an increase of Dvādaśī alone, beginning with a complete tithi, Vāsa says
mentions.role: sage whose verse prescribes fasting on Dvādaśī when Ekādaśī is elided

entities.description: Vāsa is cited as a sage-authority whose verse addresses the case where Ekādaśī is elided (consumed) and Dvādaśī extends to the next day, prescribing a fast on Dvādaśī.
entities.justification: Vāsa is explicitly named in paragraph p-620cff as the source of a verse on elided Ekādaśī and Dvādaśī fasting.

mentions.quote: As for the verse of Sāṅkhyāyana: One who has established the sacred fires, a bull, and a Brahmacārī—these three attain success by eating
mentions.role: vedic authority whose verse is cited on eating versus fasting for fire-keepers

entities.description: Sāṅkhyāyana is cited as a ritual-text authority whose verse argues that those who maintain sacred fires, bulls, and brahmacharins achieve results through eating rather than fasting.
entities.justification: Sāṅkhyāyana is explicitly named in paragraph p-fdecfa as the author of the verse on the three who succeed by eating.

mentions.quote: And the fast prompted by a Sunday, etc., is stated by Saṃvarta
mentions.role: smṛti authority whose verse enumerates auspicious occasions for fasting

entities.description: Saṃvarta is a smṛti lawgiver whose verse listing auspicious occasions (new moon, Dvādaśī, solar ingress, Sunday) and their associated rites is cited to clarify the nature of occasion-prompted versus Ekādaśī fasts.
entities.justification: Saṃvarta is explicitly named in paragraph p-44e8f0 as the authority for the verse on fasting on Sunday and other auspicious occasions.

mentions.quote: Gāndhārī fasted on one conjoined with a remainder of Daśamī. Her hundred sons were destroyed; therefore, one should avoid it
mentions.role: negative exemplar whose error of fasting on a conjoined Ekādaśī caused destruction of her hundred sons

entities.description: Gāndhārī, the Mahābhārata queen and mother of the hundred Kauravas, is cited as a negative exemplar whose mistaken fasting on a Daśamī-conjoined Ekādaśī caused the destruction of her hundred sons, illustrating the danger of the prohibited tithi.
entities.justification: Gāndhārī is explicitly named in paragraph p-a787a3 as the cautionary example for fasting on a conjoined Ekādaśī.

mentions.quote: This, conjoined with a remainder of Daśamī, was formerly given to Jambha
mentions.role: mythological figure to whom the defective conjoined Ekādaśī was assigned as a curse or trick

entities.description: Jambha is a mythological demon-figure to whom the Daśamī-conjoined Ekādaśī was 'given' in mythological time, used here as precedent for the penance required of one who inadvertently fasts on it.
entities.justification: Jambha is explicitly named in paragraph p-bdecc6 in the context of the origin of the defective conjoined Ekādaśī.

mentions.quote: the blessed Lord Hari always sleeps on the serpent-couch in the ocean of milk
mentions.role: cosmic serpent serving as Viṣṇu's bed

mentions.quote: by me who sleep on Śeṣa
mentions.role: serpent on whom Viṣṇu rests during cosmic sleep

mentions.quote: the blessed Madhusūdana attains His own illusion, the yogic sleep, on the serpent's body
mentions.role: cosmic serpent-couch for Viṣṇu's yogic sleep

entities.description: Śeṣa is the cosmic serpent on whom Viṣṇu reclines during his four-month cosmic sleep in the ocean of milk, serving as the divine couch central to the Cāturmāsya mythology.
entities.justification: Śeṣa is mentioned in paragraphs p-bb7164, p-a7d0c3, and p-1f2f28 as Viṣṇu's cosmic serpent-bed during the yogic sleep of Cāturmāsya.

mentions.quote: and on that same day, O Tāta, the Ekādaśī vow falls, or any other vow, O Skanda, what should be done then
mentions.role: deity addressed as interlocutor in śrāddha-fast conflict verse

mentions.quote: O peacock-rider! When a fast falls on the day of a śrāddha, then having performed the śrāddha, whatever is the remainder of the food
mentions.role: deity addressed in verse on how to handle conflicting obligations

entities.description: Skanda (also called Guha and the 'peacock-rider'), the war-deity and son of Śiva and Pārvatī, appears as the interlocutor in a Skanda Purāṇa verse where the dilemma of coinciding śrāddha and Ekādaśī fast is resolved.
entities.justification: Skanda is addressed by name and epithets in paragraph p-441a81 in the context of resolving a ritual conflict.

mentions.quote: Pratipad is said to be the tithi of Dhanada (Kubera) for the Pavitrāropaṇa rite
mentions.role: deity assigned to Pratipad tithi

entities.description: Kubera (called Dhanada, 'giver of wealth') is the deity of wealth assigned to Pratipad (first tithi) in a Matsya Purāṇa verse enumerating the patron deities of each tithi.
entities.justification: Kubera/Dhanada is explicitly named in paragraph p-02c03a as the deity associated with Pratipad in the tithi-deity correspondence table.

mentions.quote: Dvitīyā, the tithi of the goddess Śrī, is remembered as the best of tithis
mentions.role: goddess of prosperity assigned to Dvitīyā

entities.description: Lakṣmī, the goddess of prosperity (called Śrī), is assigned to Dvitīyā (second tithi) and called the best of tithis in the Matsya Purāṇa verse on tithi-deity correspondences.
entities.justification: Śrī/Lakṣmī is named in paragraph p-02c03a as the deity of Dvitīyā in the tithi enumeration.

mentions.quote: Tṛtīyā is of Bhavānī, and Caturthī of her son
mentions.role: goddess assigned to Tṛtīyā tithi

entities.description: Bhavānī (Pārvatī, consort of Śiva) is the deity of Tṛtīyā (third tithi) in the Matsya Purāṇa's tithi-deity table; her son (Gaṇeśa) is assigned to Caturthī.
entities.justification: Bhavānī is named in paragraph p-02c03a in the tithi-deity correspondence verse.

mentions.quote: Caturthī of her son
mentions.role: deity assigned to Caturthī tithi

entities.description: Gaṇeśa, son of Bhavānī (Pārvatī), is the deity assigned to Caturthī (fourth tithi) in the Matsya Purāṇa verse on tithi-deity correspondences.
entities.justification: Gaṇeśa ('her son') is named in paragraph p-02c03a in the tithi-deity enumeration.

mentions.quote: Pañcamī is of Dharmarāja, and Ṣaṣṭhī of Guha
mentions.role: deity of Pañcamī tithi

entities.description: Dharmarāja (a title of Yama as upholder of dharma) is assigned to Pañcamī (fifth tithi) in the Matsya Purāṇa tithi-deity table.
entities.justification: Dharmarāja is named in paragraph p-02c03a in the tithi-deity correspondence verse.

mentions.quote: Saptamī is said to be of Bhāskara (the sun)
mentions.role: solar deity assigned to Saptamī

mentions.quote: in the month of Jyeṣṭha, in the bright fortnight, on Daśamī, with Wednesday and Hasta, in the Garā, Ānanda, and Vyatīpāta yogas, with the moon in Virgo and the sun in Taurus
mentions.role: astronomical body whose position marks the special Daśaharā yoga

entities.description: Sūrya (the sun god, called Bhāskara 'the illuminator') is the deity of Saptamī tithi and appears as an astronomical reference point in the Daśaharā yoga passage.
entities.justification: Bhāskara/Sūrya is named in the tithi-deity verse in paragraph p-02c03a and appears astronomically in paragraph p-8caf4f.

mentions.quote: Daśamī is said to be of Vāsuki
mentions.role: serpent-deity assigned to Daśamī tithi

entities.description: Vāsuki, the king of serpents, is assigned to Daśamī (tenth tithi) in the Matsya Purāṇa's tithi-deity correspondence table.
entities.justification: Vāsuki is explicitly named in paragraph p-02c03a in the tithi-deity enumeration.

mentions.quote: Trayodaśī is of Anaṅga (Kāma)
mentions.role: deity of love assigned to Trayodaśī

entities.description: Kāma (the god of love, called Anaṅga 'the bodiless one') is the deity of Trayodaśī in the Matsya Purāṇa tithi-deity table.
entities.justification: Kāma/Anaṅga is named in paragraph p-02c03a in the tithi-deity verse.

mentions.quote: from the yugma-vākya 'conjoined with Rudra (11th) is Dvādaśī'
mentions.role: deity identified with Ekādaśī through the number eleven (Rudra)

mentions.quote: Saptamī conjoined with Śiva
mentions.role: deity associated with nakṣatra-conjuncted tithi prohibition

mentions.quote: Caturdaśī is said to be of Śiva
mentions.role: deity assigned to Caturdaśī tithi

entities.description: Śiva (also called Rudra, a name identifying him with the eleven Rudras) is referenced as the deity of Caturdaśī and appears in tithi-prohibitions and the yugma-vākya formula linking Ekādaśī to Dvādaśī.
entities.justification: Śiva/Rudra is named in paragraphs p-87167f, p-8216ce, and p-02c03a in tithi-deity and fasting-prohibition contexts.

mentions.quote: the gods, with Indra, go and awaken the Lord of gods
mentions.role: king of gods who leads the divine assembly in awakening Viṣṇu at Kārtika Ekādaśī

entities.description: Indra, king of the gods, leads the divine assembly that awakens Viṣṇu from his four-month yogic sleep at the Ekādaśī of Kārtika, as described in the Viṣṇudharmottara.
entities.justification: Indra is explicitly named in paragraph p-4bd59a as leading the gods who awaken Viṣṇu at Kārtika Ekādaśī.

mentions.quote: the sleeping one is attended by ṛṣis equal to Brahmā
mentions.role: deity invoked as standard of comparison for the attending sages

mentions.quote: And Paurṇamāsī, O best of sages, is remembered as my tithi
mentions.role: deity claiming the full moon day as his own tithi

entities.description: Brahmā, the creator deity, appears as the standard of comparison for the ṛṣis attending Viṣṇu's sleep and as the speaker-deity who claims Paurṇamāsī (full moon) as his own tithi.
entities.justification: Brahmā appears in paragraphs p-4bd59a and p-02c03a in contexts of Viṣṇu's sleep attendants and the tithi-deity table.

mentions.quote: Janārdana is praised by the gods, ṛṣis, and hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases
mentions.role: celestial musicians praising Viṣṇu at Āṣāḍha Ekādaśī

entities.description: The Gandharvas are celestial musicians who, along with gods, ṛṣis, and Apsarases, praise Janārdana (Viṣṇu) for five days beginning with the bright Ekādaśī of Āṣāḍha.
entities.justification: The Gandharvas are named in paragraph p-97472b as one of the groups performing the five-day festival for Viṣṇu.

mentions.quote: hosts of Gandharvas and Apsarases
mentions.role: celestial dancers praising Viṣṇu at Āṣāḍha Ekādaśī

entities.description: The Apsarases are celestial nymphs who participate in the five-day festival of song and dance in praise of Viṣṇu at Āṣāḍha Ekādaśī alongside gods, ṛṣis, and Gandharvas.
entities.justification: The Apsarases are named in paragraph p-97472b as participants in the divine festival for Viṣṇu's sleep.

mentions.quote: Navamī is of the Mātṛs
mentions.role: group of mother-goddesses assigned to Navamī

entities.description: The Mātṛs (the divine Mothers, a group of goddess-energies) are assigned to Navamī (ninth tithi) in the Matsya Purāṇa's tithi-deity table.
entities.justification: The Mātṛs are explicitly named in paragraph p-02c03a as the deities of Navamī.

mentions.quote: by those devoted to Viṣṇu
mentions.role: category of practitioners with specific ritual obligations

mentions.quote: And this is for those other than Vaiṣṇavas
mentions.role: group for whom a specific dark Ekādaśī exception does not apply

mentions.quote: And this aruṇodaya-vedha is only for Vaiṣṇavas
mentions.role: group for whom dawn-conjunction vedha applies

mentions.quote: A Vaiṣṇava is one who has received initiation into a Viṣṇu mantra
mentions.role: defined category of Viṣṇu-initiates

mentions.quote: It is undisputed that an Ekādaśī conjoined at dawn should always be rejected by Vaiṣṇavas
mentions.role: group for whom the conjoined Ekādaśī is unambiguously forbidden

entities.description: Vaiṣṇavas—defined as those who have received initiation into a Viṣṇu mantra—form a distinct ritual category with stricter Ekādaśī rules (aruṇodaya-vedha applies, both fortnights obligatory) compared to Smārtas.
entities.justification: Vaiṣṇavas are defined and distinguished from Smārtas throughout the Ekādaśī determination section, beginning with paragraph p-458f82.

mentions.quote: Now, for Smārtas
mentions.role: distinct ritual category with different Ekādaśī rules from Vaiṣṇavas

mentions.quote: Therein, Ekādaśī, though of two kinds by the division of pure and conjoined, is of nine kinds for each
mentions.role: group for whom the eighteen-fold Ekādaśī classification applies

entities.description: Smārtas are practitioners following smṛti tradition (as opposed to Vaiṣṇava āgamic initiation), for whom the Ekādaśī determination is more complex, involving an eighteen-fold classification based on the lengths of Ekādaśī and Dvādaśī.
entities.justification: Smārtas are explicitly distinguished from Vaiṣṇavas starting at paragraph p-269e82 and given their own detailed Ekādaśī rules.

mentions.quote: On the Daśamī of the bright fortnight, in the month of Jyeṣṭha, on a Tuesday, in the Hasta nakṣatra, the pure river descended from heaven
mentions.role: sacred river whose heavenly descent marks Daśaharā

entities.description: Gaṅgā, the sacred river descended from heaven, whose descent on the Daśamī of Jyeṣṭha is the mythological event commemorated by Daśaharā, the festival that removes ten sins.
entities.justification: The Gaṅgā's descent is the defining mythological event of Daśaharā, described in paragraph p-8caf4f from the Skanda Purāṇa.

themes.topic: Tithi determination: rules for accepting a tithi when it spans two days

mentions.quote: the performance of an optional rite on a divided tithi is prohibited
For Daśamī, there is no such regulating verse. Therefore, if Daśamī pervades the time of the rite on both days, either the preceding or the succeeding day may be taken by choice
an option is flawed by eight faults, and it is improper for mere human choice to prevail, some regulating scripture must necessarily be accepted

themes.justification: The digest's primary legal-hermeneutic task throughout this window is determining which day to take when a tithi spans two calendar days, applying Mīmāṃsā principles to reconcile conflicting Purāṇic verses.

themes.topic: Cāturmāsya and the cosmic sleep of Viṣṇu: ritual structure of the four-month vow

mentions.quote: On the bright Ekādaśī of Āṣāḍha, the blessed Lord Hari always sleeps on the serpent-couch in the ocean of milk
On this same bright Ekādaśī of Āṣāḍha, the commencement of the Cāturmāsya vow is stated in the Mahābhārata
He sleeps for four months, until Kārttikī arrives. During that time, special rites such as sacrifices are not performed

themes.justification: The Cāturmāsya section (paragraphs around p-bb7164 through p-3d3d39) explores the theology and ritual timing of Viṣṇu's four-month cosmic sleep and its associated ceremonies of sleep, turning-over, and awakening.

themes.topic: Ekādaśī fasting rights: differentiation by social category (householder, renunciant, widow, woman, Vaiṣṇava, Smārta)

mentions.quote: In the vow, however, in its obligatory performance, those other than householders have the right in both fortnights. But a householder has it only in the bright fortnight
And this should be performed by a widow in both fortnights
it is flawless that a married woman, like a householder, has the right only on the bright fortnight

themes.justification: The Ekādaśī section systematically differentiates fasting obligations by social and ritual category, a central organizational theme of dharmaśāstra.

themes.topic: Vedha (ritual contamination by adjacent tithi): aruṇodaya-vedha vs. sūryodaya-vedha

mentions.quote: The Ekādaśī that is conjoined with the two muhūrtas before the time of sunrise is complete; the other is declared to be conjoined
If the dawn is conjoined with Daśamī, it should not be fasted on by a Vaiṣṇava; that is not the Ekādaśī vow
the aruṇodaya-vedha is also for everyone, because of the general statement on conjunction

themes.justification: The concept of vedha—contamination of a tithi by contact with an adjacent tithi at dawn or sunrise—is a central technical theme running through the entire Ekādaśī section.

themes.topic: Conflict resolution between simultaneous ritual obligations using Mīmāṃsā hermeneutics

mentions.quote: a resolve is enjoined by metaphorical interpretation (lakṣaṇā). The censure of eating there, by the maxim 'censure does not proceed to censure,' is for the praise of the vow
When a fast is obligatory (nitya), and a śrāddha is occasional (naimittika), one should then perform the fast, having smelled what has been offered to the ancestors
the truth, however, is that by the maxim 'a mention of a fruit for a subordinate element is an explanatory statement'

themes.justification: Throughout this window, the Vīramitrodaya applies Mīmāṃsā interpretive principles (lakṣaṇā, paryudāsa, arthavāda, the nitya-naimittika hierarchy) to resolve conflicts between injunctions.

themes.topic: Nakṣatra-tithi conjunctions as determinants of ritual timing

mentions.quote: the Navamī conjoined with the three nakṣatras beginning with Mūla is declared to be great
Viṣṇu sleeps in the first quarter of Maitra (Anurādhā), turns over in the middle of Śruti (Śravaṇa), and the slayer of the Suras' enemies awakens at the end of Pauṣṇa (Revatī)
If Daśamī is present for a little at sunrise, and Ekādaśī is complete, at the time when it is in the Śravaṇa nakṣatra, that tithi is called Vijayā

themes.justification: The specific combination of tithi and nakṣatra is a recurring technical determinant throughout this window, shaping which day is chosen for Navamī, Daśamī, and Ekādaśī observances.

themes.topic: Scriptural hierarchy: smṛti vs. śruti vs. Purāṇa and the principle of analogical extension

mentions.quote: An optional (kāmya) fast, however, supersedes even the obligatory śrauta Agnihotra, etc., because the strength of the object of the injunction is greater than the strength of the authority
because the Agnihotra, etc., are śrauta (based on śruti), it is proper that they should supersede the smārta (based on smṛti) cessation of eating

themes.justification: The text implicitly develops a hierarchy in which śrauta rites generally supersede smārta ones, but obligatory smārta fasts coexist with obligatory śrauta rites, and optional rites of any category can override obligatory ones of lower authority.

themes.topic: Festival calendar: Navamī, Daśamī, Ekādaśī, and their named observances

mentions.quote: The Navamī of the bright fortnight of Āśvina is Durgā-navamī; it is also Mahānavamī
The Daśamī of the bright fortnight of Jyeṣṭha is Daśaharā
The Daśamī of the bright fortnight of Āśvina is Vijayā-daśamī

themes.justification: The window systematically covers the named festival observances for Navamī through Ekādaśī—Durgā-navamī/Mahānavamī, Daśaharā, Vijayā-daśamī, the Cāturmāsya vow—organized by tithi.

themes.topic: Women's ritual agency: dependence on husband's permission and differential Ekādaśī rights

mentions.quote: The woman who, while her husband is alive, performs a fast or a vow, shortens the life of her husband and goes to hell
A wife should always perform vows, etc., only with the consent of her husband
it is flawless that a married woman, like a householder, has the right only on the bright fortnight

themes.justification: The window contains an explicit sub-discussion of women's ritual rights, conditioning fasting on husbandly consent and distinguishing widows (both fortnights) from married women (bright fortnight only).

citations.quote: And so, in the Bhaviṣya Purāṇa: The Aṣṭamī of the bright fortnight of Āṣvayuj, conjoined with Mūla, is named Mahānavamī
citations.justification: The Bhaviṣya Purāṇa is cited as a scriptural authority on the identification of Mahānavamī.

citations.quote: And so, in the Padma Purāṇa: Śrāvaṇī, Durgā-navamī, Dūrvā, and Hutāśanī, Śivarātri, and the day of Bali should be performed when conjoined with the preceding day
citations.justification: The Padma Purāṇa is cited as authoritative for the rule that Durgā-navamī should be taken when conjoined with the preceding day.

citations.quote: And from the Skānda Purāṇa: One should never perform Navamī, O Tāta, when it is conjoined with Daśamī
citations.justification: The Skanda Purāṇa is cited on the prohibition of performing Navamī when conjoined with Daśamī.

citations.quote: This is from the Devī Purāṇa
citations.justification: The Devī Purāṇa is cited for verses on the animal sacrifice timing relative to Aṣṭamī and Navamī.

citations.quote: This is from the Saura Purāṇa. This also pertains only to the animal sacrifice
citations.justification: The Saura Purāṇa is cited for a verse on the completeness of Navamī for animal sacrifice purposes.

citations.quote: the Madanaratna says it is a prohibition when the tithi is pure and of increased duration
citations.justification: The Madanaratna (a dharmaśāstra digest) is cited for interpreting Nārada's verse as a prohibition applying only to pure and extended tithis.

citations.quote: Beginning with it, in the Purāṇasamuccaya: On Daśamī, men should properly worship Aparājitā, facing the northeast direction, in the afternoon, with effort
citations.justification: The Purāṇasamuccaya is cited as the source for the Vijayā-daśamī worship prescription.

citations.quote: This is from the Skanda Purāṇa. 'Complete' means on both days
citations.justification: The Skanda Purāṇa is cited for the rule that a complete Daśamī may be taken on either day.

citations.quote: This is stated in the Skanda Purāṇa itself. 'With Durgā' means conjoined with Navamī
citations.justification: The Skanda Purāṇa is cited again for the rule that Daśamī should be performed conjoined with Navamī.

citations.quote: in the Kūrma Purāṇa. Here, Pūrṇā = Daśamī. It is understood that when conjoined with Nandā = Ekādaśī, it is fruitless
citations.justification: The Kūrma Purāṇa is cited for the verse identifying the paraviddhā Daśamī-Ekādaśī conjunction as fruitless.

citations.quote: This is in the Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa
citations.justification: The Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa is cited for prohibiting fasting on several tithis including Daśamī when conjoined with the succeeding day.

citations.quote: These verses in the Śivarahasya, Saurapurāṇa, etc., apply only to the dark fortnight, not to cases of pervasion
citations.justification: The Śivarahasya is cited (and its applicability limited) in the discussion of Ṣaṣṭhī-Nāga and Saptamī-Śiva conjunction prohibitions.

citations.quote: This is from the Skanda Purāṇa
citations.justification: The Skanda Purāṇa is cited for the verse on the descent of the Gaṅgā marking Daśaharā.

citations.quote: This is from the Brahma Purāṇa, in that context
citations.justification: The Brahma Purāṇa is cited for the prescription of Vāstu-pūjana by Vaiśyas on the bright Ekādaśī of Caitra.

citations.quote: Therein, in the Brahma Purāṇa
citations.justification: The Brahma Purāṇa is cited for the injunction of Viṣṇu's sleep on the bright Ekādaśī of Āṣāḍha and awakening on Kārtika Ekādaśī.

citations.quote: In the Bhaviṣyottara also: When the month of Bhādrapada has arrived, on the day of the bright Ekādaśī, the turning of the side of Viṣṇu occurs
citations.justification: The Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇa is cited for the turning-of-the-side (Pārśvaikādaśī) observance in Bhādrapada.

citations.quote: In the Varāha Purāṇa, etc., however, the sleep, etc., are stated for the bright Dvādaśīs of these same months
citations.justification: The Varāha Purāṇa is cited as an alternative tradition placing Viṣṇu's sleep ceremonies on Dvādaśī rather than Ekādaśī.

citations.quote: It would also contradict this verse of the Matsya Purāṇa
citations.justification: The Matsya Purāṇa is cited for the tithi-deity correspondence table (Dvādaśī belongs to Viṣṇu) used to refute the identification of Āṣāḍhī as Ekādaśī.

citations.quote: the interpretation of the Kalpataru, that Āṣāḍhī is Ekādaśī, and Kārttikī is Ekādaśī, is refuted
citations.justification: The Kalpataru (another dharmaśāstra digest) is explicitly cited and then refuted by the Vīramitrodaya for its interpretation that Āṣāḍhī and Kārttikī refer to Ekādaśī rather than the full moon.

citations.quote: And in the Viṣṇudharmottara, it is clearly stated 'at the end of the fortnight'
citations.justification: The Viṣṇudharmottara is cited to confirm that the full moon (end of fortnight) is one valid time for Viṣṇu's sleep ceremony.

citations.quote: In the Viṣṇudharmottara, however, the sleep and awakening are stated for a period of five days beginning with Ekādaśī
citations.justification: The Viṣṇudharmottara is also cited for the five-day festival beginning on Ekādaśī as yet another alternative time.

citations.quote: This is from the Bhaviṣya Purāṇa
citations.justification: The Bhaviṣya Purāṇa is cited for the prescription that Viṣṇu sleeps at night, awakens during the day, and turns over at twilight.

citations.quote: This is also from the Viṣṇudharmottara
citations.justification: The Viṣṇudharmottara is cited to confirm that Viṣṇu does not sleep during the day or awaken at night.

citations.quote: And so, in the Bhaviṣya Purāṇa: Viṣṇu sleeps in the first quarter of Maitra (Anurādhā)
citations.justification: The Bhaviṣya Purāṇa is cited for the nakṣatra-based timing of Viṣṇu's sleep, turning, and awakening.

citations.quote: This is from a verse of the Varāha Purāṇa
citations.justification: The Varāha Purāṇa is cited for the rule that when nakṣatra-quarter conjunction is absent, the nakṣatra alone suffices for timing the sleep ceremonies.

citations.quote: And so, in the Varāha Purāṇa: On Dvādaśī, at the time of the junction, when there is no possibility of the nakṣatras
citations.justification: The Varāha Purāṇa is cited again for the fallback rule of performing sleep ceremonies at twilight on Dvādaśī when no nakṣatra conjunction is available.

citations.quote: On this same bright Ekādaśī of Āṣāḍha, the commencement of the Cāturmāsya vow is stated in the Mahābhārata
citations.justification: The Mahābhārata is cited as an epic authority prescribing the commencement of the Cāturmāsya vow on Āṣāḍha bright Ekādaśī.

citations.quote: Therein, in verses such as this from the Nāradīya: In every fortnight, a fast should be performed on Ekādaśī
citations.justification: The Nāradīya Purāṇa is cited for the general injunction to fast on Ekādaśī every fortnight.

citations.quote: This is from the Agni Purāṇa
citations.justification: The Agni Purāṇa is cited for the injunction that householders, brahmacharins, and those with established fires should not eat on Ekādaśī in either fortnight.

citations.quote: This is also from the prohibition of a pūrvaviddhā tithi in the Skanda Purāṇa and Bhaviṣya Purāṇa
citations.justification: Both the Skanda Purāṇa and Bhaviṣya Purāṇa are cited for prohibiting Ekādaśī conjoined with Daśamī.

citations.quote: This is also from the Bhaviṣyottara
citations.justification: The Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇa is cited for the verse distinguishing householders (bright Ekādaśī only) from brahmacharins and women (both fortnights).

citations.quote: This is also from the Bhaviṣya Purāṇa
citations.justification: The Bhaviṣya Purāṇa is cited for distinguishing bright and dark Ekādaśī fasting by householders (bright, for enjoyment) vs. liberation-seekers (dark).

citations.quote: From these verses of the Nāradīya and Tattvasāgara, it is understood that he should fast on all dark Ekādaśīs
citations.justification: The Tattvasāgara is cited alongside the Nāradīya as authority for the Vaiṣṇava obligation to fast on all Ekādaśīs including dark fortnight.

citations.quote: This is from the Gāruḍa Purāṇa
citations.justification: The Gāruḍa Purāṇa is cited for the rule that a Vaiṣṇava should not fast on an Ekādaśī conjoined with Daśamī at dawn.

citations.quote: This is from the Gāruḍa Purāṇa
citations.justification: The Gāruḍa Purāṇa is cited again for the rule on 'doubtful Ekādaśī' (vedha of three ghaṭikās before sunrise) and the prescription to fast on Dvādaśī instead.

citations.quote: This is from the Bhaviṣya Purāṇa. 'Moon' (soma) = Ekādaśī
citations.justification: The Bhaviṣya Purāṇa is cited for the rule on increasing/decreasing Ekādaśī and the vedha rule adjustment.

citations.quote: This is from the Viṣṇurahasya
citations.justification: The Viṣṇurahasya is cited for the conditional rule on fasting on a Daśamī-conjoined Ekādaśī depending on Dvādaśī extension into Trayodaśī.

citations.quote: For this very reason, in the Skanda Purāṇa: All the tithis, beginning with Pratipad, from one sunrise of the sun to the next, are known as complete, with the exception of Harivāsara (Ekādaśī)
citations.justification: The Skanda Purāṇa is cited for the definition of completeness for all tithis, with the explicit exception of Ekādaśī (Harivāsara).

citations.quote: As for the Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa: Four ghaṭikās in the morning are desired as the dawn
citations.justification: The Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa is cited for the definition of aruṇodaya (dawn) as four ghaṭikās before sunrise.

citations.quote: This is also from the Viṣṇudharmottara
citations.justification: The Viṣṇudharmottara is cited for the rule that nakṣatra quarter conjunction, not the nakṣatra itself, is not the determining cause when Dvādaśī is involved.

citations.quote: He who has received the initiation stated in the Vaikhānasa and other āgamas is a Vaiṣṇava
citations.justification: The Vaikhanāsa Āgama is cited as the defining scriptural source for what constitutes a Vaiṣṇava (one who has received Viṣṇu-mantra initiation).

citations.quote: This is also from the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa. Here, the mention of father, etc., applies to a case where the husband is not present
citations.justification: The Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa is cited for the rule that a woman's vow performed without permission of husband, father, or son is fruitless.

citations.quote: This is also from the Skanda Purāṇa
citations.justification: The Skanda Purāṇa is cited for the detailed resolution of śrāddha-Ekādaśī conflict (smelling leftover food to satisfy both obligations).

citations.quote: This is from the Bhaviṣya Purāṇa
citations.justification: The Bhaviṣya Purāṇa is cited for the complete Ekādaśī definition (conjoined with two muhūrtas before sunrise).

citations.quote: And also in the Bhaviṣya Purāṇa cited by Hemādri: On the Dvādaśī of the bright fortnight are the festivals of sleep and turning over
citations.justification: Hemādri's citation of the Bhaviṣya Purāṇa is referenced as an additional authority for the Dvādaśī placement of sleep festivals.
